clue.text: Organised parties walk wearily

indicators.note: something organised has been put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Groups of revellers on organised outings trudge along, tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge somewhere tiredly or reluctantly, a synonym for plodding along.

clue.text: Make an effort to accommodate old party member

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house or take in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: to try is to make an effort
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An appeal to find room for a veteran member of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory belongs to the Conservative Party, so is a member of a political party.

clue.text: Ewan's drunk again!

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the name without its 's, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that Ewan has had too much once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', so Ewan is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means once more or afresh, the same sense as again.

clue.text: Brave infants, backed by mother

blocks.note: surface: courageous little children
setter's reading: babies of a Native American brave, carried on the mother's back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective for plucky toddlers, but it is the old word for a Native American warrior, and 'backed' is literal: these babies ride on mum's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a Native American baby, traditionally carried on its mother's back in a cradleboard.

clue.text: High spot for Jane around one

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the name wraps the other piece

blocks.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's heroine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A high point in someone named Jane's life.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane here is the heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel, not just any Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a cliff or treetop, so a lofty spot.

clue.text: Summary is not entirely accurate

indicators.note: not the whole word, so its final letter is cut off

blocks.note: accurate means exact or precise

explanation.surface: A complaint that a summary does not quite get things right.
explanation.walkthrough: PRECISE loses its last letter to leave PRECIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A precis is a short abridged version of a text giving its main points.

clue.text: Make allusion about ingestion of ecstasy and marijuana

indicators.note: ingesting something takes it inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: to refer to something is to allude to it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone hints at having taken ecstasy and cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside REFER: RE(E)FER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a cannabis cigarette, slang associated with the drug itself.

clue.text: Give in to a cute plait, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged some other way

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone yields to the charm of a sweet braid of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to surrender or yield to an opponent.

clue.text: Positions a marksman inside the communication device

definitions.note: singular in the clue, plural answer

indicators.note: inside means within, so the middle pieces sit in the outer word

blocks.note: sites are positions or locations
taken as written
William Tell, the Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: A sniper is stationed inside some telecom equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The marksman is the legendary Swiss archer. The clue's singular 'device' does not quite match the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellites in orbit relay telephone, television and data signals around the Earth.

clue.text: Former partner shot out to to get things sent abroad again

indicators.note: one item is sent out to sit within the other, so one goes inside the other

blocks.note: a report is the bang of a gunshot
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is shot, while elsewhere goods are being shipped overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a killing, but it is the bang a gun makes. The printed clue has a doubled 'to'; the wordplay is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-export is to ship imported goods out of the country once more.

clue.text: Order posted by tyrant

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An order that has been posted up by a tyrannical ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a noun, a decree; it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, a synonym for tyrant.

clue.text: One new day, one court charge

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
D is the abbreviation for day
I is the Roman numeral one
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A fresh day brings a single charge in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict is to formally accuse someone of a crime, a sense of charge.

clue.text: Queen Victoria gone flipping mad in the world of power

indicators.note: flipping can mean tossing or turning over, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: VR, Victoria Regina, was Queen Victoria's royal cipher
taken as written
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria has gone flipping mad, a scandal in the corridors of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British oath intensifying 'mad', but it is the anagram signal for VR plus GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Governmental describes things relating to government, the sphere in which state power is held.

clue.text: Role subtly played by public transport

indicators.note: something played is performed in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor gives an understated performance as part of a bus company advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtly' looks like part of the indicator, describing how the role is played, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus is an electric bus drawing power from overhead wires, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Felt listless, having been in front when invasive agony occurred

indicators.note: something invasive pushes its way in, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: someone who was in front of the field led
anguish is severe pain or agony

explanation.surface: A competitor lost all energy after leading, once a sharp pain set in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having been in front' is a past tense verb, matching the past tense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to grow weak or lose vitality, so languished means felt lethargic.

clue.text: Praised her extravagantly for getting the university post

indicators.note: done extravagantly means wildly and without restraint, so these letters run wild

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gushed over a colleague to help her land an academic job.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A readership is the academic position held by a reader at a British university.

clue.text: Girl raised money from Albania for settler in Israel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a girl
the lek is Albania's currency

explanation.surface: A young woman raised funds from Albania for someone who settled in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist, but here it is whatever settles a bill: Israel's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The shekel is the Israeli currency, the thing used to settle debts there.

clue.text: Flowers found regularly in Algeria

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A botanical note that some flowers grow commonly across Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: The Spanish tango involved energy, so pull out

indicators.note: something involved is intricate and tangled, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
taken as written, to be rearranged
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Spanish tango took so much energy that someone had to withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to stretch or draw something out so it becomes longer.

clue.text: A record would, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: the word sounds like timber, and a cut length of timber from a tree is this

explanation.surface: A wistful-sounding fragment: a record would, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Would' sounds like wood, and the answer is a piece of wood as well as a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A log is a written record of events, such as a ship's logbook.

clue.text: In the middle I set fire to a small amount of liquid

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the middle is the centre
taken as written
to light something is to set fire to it

explanation.surface: A confession of having started a fire right in the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the middle' looks like a position for the whole phrase, but 'In' is the container signal and 'the middle' supplies letters; the answer uses the British spelling of litre.
explanation.definitionFit: A centilitre is one hundredth of a litre, a tiny measure of liquid.

clue.text: Put money on everyone coming inside for the dance

indicators.note: coming inside means entering, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to bet is to put money on an outcome
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone gambles as the whole crowd comes indoors for the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a classical theatrical form of dance.

clue.text: Miss Doolittle, a little woman, had the answer — Leicester and Essex

blocks.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady
Beth is one of the March sisters in Little Women
ans is a standard abbreviation of answer

explanation.surface: Two fictional women solve a puzzle whose solution is the names of two English places.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester and Essex here are not places but the Earls of Leicester and Essex, favourites of Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley and Robert Devereux were courtiers of Elizabeth I's reign, so both were people of that era.

clue.text: A dropout with large thighs?

blocks.note: first meaning: a counterculture rebel who rejects conventional society
second meaning: broad in the hips

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the second sense is the adjective from hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a flower child who opts out of society, and an adjective for someone with wide hips.

clue.text: Sort of benevolent

blocks.note: first meaning: a type or variety
second meaning: generous and caring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reads as a hedge meaning rather; it splits into a noun and a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a type or category; as an adjective it means considerate and generous.

clue.text: Matured like a good journalist

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
ed is short for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: Someone has grown up to resemble a fine reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means grown older or ripened, as wine or cheese is matured.

clue.text: Saw man left in plot

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it, so the earlier pieces sit within the last

blocks.note: a plot of ground for planting is a bed
he is the pronoun for a man
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a man abandoned in a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a scheme, but here it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, an old word for to see or look at.

clue.text: Giving a contemporary look, when riding out with someone

blocks.note: a jockey who is riding a horse is said to be up
going out with someone romantically is dating them

explanation.surface: Smartening oneself up for a ride out with a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Updating something means modernising it so it suits the present day.

clue.text: Keep quiet and demure

blocks.note: first meaning: to calm someone with a drug, a verb
second meaning: calm and composed, an adjective

explanation.surface: Advice to stay silent and modest.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means calm with a tranquilliser; as an adjective it means staid and unhurried.

clue.text: Returned and gave in

blocks.note: first meaning: produced as profit or harvest
second meaning: surrendered or conceded

explanation.surface: Someone came back and surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment that produced a return has yielded; someone who submitted to pressure has also yielded.
